AGRIZZI - THE MONEY AND THE ESCAPE PLAN

By: Nicky Troll | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Agrizzi - from whistleblower to inmate - we look at the hidden money and the escape plan

Summary:
2019 – Corruptor turned Whistleblower Agrizzi blows the lid off deep-rooted bribery and corruption that build the billion rand facilities management company Bosasa. His testimony at the Zondo Commission left South Africans conflicted - was he a rogue or a hero for speaking out.
2020 – Agrizzi is arrested and charged for a second time. This time no bail. He is behind bars awaiting trial.

We do a piece looking at why Agrizzi has been denied bail. We unpack the lies about the money. We look at the HAWKS investigation that foiled Agrizzi’s alleged escape plan to Italy.

Further information:
SOME DETAILS:
Agrizzi was shipping millions to offshore accounts and had already bought a luxury house and vehicle in Italy – using his wife as the “money mule” – they are legally divorced – but still together. Agrizzi also allegedly transferred millions of rands to crypto currency account and sold off assets including luxury Ferrari sports cars.

Adding to Agrizzi’s trouble - the Hawks established that he had been defaulting on his R13.5m bond and was owing a local bank R8.1m.

THE ESCAPE PLAN
Former Bosasa chief operating officer Angelo Agrizzi got himself into trouble with the Hawks due to his planned trip to Italy in July, but Deputy Chief Justice Raymond Zondo saved the situation by blocking the alleged escape.
Agrizzi’s alleged plot to flee to Italy and live a life of luxury beyond the borders of South Africa is contained in the affidavit of Lieutenant-Colonel Bernadus Lazarus - presented in court this week.
In his affidavit, Lieutenant-Colonel Lazarus said he became aware of the planned escape after Agrizzi informed him of his intention to travel in July.
Lazarus said what raised his alarm was that Agrizzi’s did not ask for his SA passport but insisted on undertaking his trip. The court heard the two things saved the trip - one of them being Judge Zondo.
The Judge, according to evidence in court, had served Agrizzi with a summons to be around when former Gauteng premier Nomvula Mokonyane appears before the commission to rebut allegations that she too benefited financially from Bosasa.
The Hawks, the court heard, were satisfied that the summons prevented Agrizzi’s from undertaking his trip. The other reasons presented was that South Africa was still under Covid-19 level 3 which prevented any international trips.
INTERVIEWS
 Dawie Roodt – how the money flowed out of the country and what it means in terms of recovering the assets.
 The HAWKS – they’ve already testified in the bail hearing and giving a detailed affidavit as to what transpired in terms of hiding money and the escape plan. It’s already public record – nice opportunity for the HAWKs to claim so positive publicity.
 Manie Wits, S.C. – Agrizzi’s lawyer – he has commented in the media as well and will respond to RoRs for Agrizzi and his wife.
 Mandy Weiner – she’ll help us tell the story of Agrizzi and has written a book – The Whistleblowers – those who expose, pay hugely – she touches on the Agrizzi case and has written extensitvely about Bosasa.

Script:


STRUCTURE

VO: With a string of arrests across the country in recent weeks - the NPA and the HAWKS are on a mission, to bring those implicated in corruption to book,

Amongst those appearing in the dock on corruption charges, were former top ANC MP Vincent Smith and Former Bosasa COO Angelo Agrizzi – who exposed deep-rooted bribery and corruption, that built the billion rand Bosasa Empire, that thrived off government tenders.

LINK: The thing with Whistleblowing is that you don’t know how it’s going to play out – with you be seen as a hero speaking up, a rogue trying to avoid the heat or in handcuffs behind bars.
VO: Agrizzi’s explosive testimony at the Zondo Commission in 2019 left South Africans conflicted about his motives.
Specialist crime journalist and author, Mandy Wiener, explains there is always risk attached to whistleblowing – whether the intention for speaking out is altruistic virtuous, accidental or for simply for survival.

MANDY: on the far end you've got whistleblowers who have a proximity to wrongdoing. They were involved in wrongdoing themselves and they may have a Damascus moment they may decide for self-preservation to to speak up and Angela Agrizzi falls into that category. M4

UPSOUND 2019 STORY
A - I never corrupted anybody… I was a facilitator…yes // I betrayed myself, my family – the people looked up to – should have done it 20 years

VO: Agrizzi named and shamed the alleged corrupted – the list is long including Dudu Myeni, Nomvula Mokonyane, Gwede Mantashe, NPA staff, members of parliament; senior correctional services officials and former President Jacob Zuma.

He even alleged that bribe money was packed in Bosasa’s vaults. This video shows now deceased Bosasa CEO, Gavin Watson inside.

UPSOUND BOSASA 2019
UPSOUND CLIP “…. eight…nine.. A million exactly…”

A - you got keep paying people // if you don’t do it this person is going to they will be anti us

VO: The alleged bribery extended to paid holidays, security systems, home renovations and even Christmas Groceries ranging from booze to frozen chicken and braai packs.

Claims that are denied by some those implicated:
UPSOUND GWEDE CALL

VO: It was alleged that Dudu Myeni was the go between for cash intended for the Jacob Zuma Foundation.

UPSOUND DUDE CALL: Agrizzi never impiclated DM – I don’t know what is expected of me….

VO: While Mokonyane and former Presiden Jacob Zuma couldn’t be reached for comment, both appeared before the Zondo Commission and denied the allegations.
VO: Agrizzi’s bombshell testimony hasn’t just made him unpopular in political circles, it’s also led to criminal charges.
In 2019, he was charged with fraud, conspiracy to commit fraud, corruption and money laundering - alongside former correctional services commissioner Linda Mti , former CFO of correctional services Patrick Gillingham , and Bosasa’s former CFO Andries Van Tonder . At the time, they were all released on bail.
Despite various attempts, Mti could not be reached, both Gillingham and Van Tonder declined to comment.

Fast forward to 2020. New corruption charges linked to Vincent Smith. And bail denied for Agrizzi this time round.

A move that caught even his legal team off guard in light of Agrizzi’s state of health explains his attorney Daniel Witz,

DANIEL: It wasn't taken into cognizance and thereafter when he was admitted into the Jo'burg Central Prison his health deteriorated even further due to his comorbidities. M3

VO: While Agrizzi is still remanded in custody, he has been transferred from the prison hospital to a private facility.

LINK: When Agrizzi was before the Zondo commission – we thought we were given insights to all the dodgy dealings – but it seems now there was whole subplot unfolding

MANDY: the decision by the NPA to oppose bail and for him to now be behind bars is a clear indication that they no longer trust him and that they feel that he is the primary accused in this matter M8

VO: The State opposed bail on the grounds that Agrizzi had not been honest in declaring all of his assets.

In the (6) February 2019 affidavit filed in support of the first bail application, Agrizzi stated:

“My wife and I own movable assets valued at approaimately R2 650 000.00 and immovable property valued at approxiamtely R14 000 000.00”

The HAWKS investigation contradicts this statement. According to the affidavit of Lt Col Bernard Lazarus, Agrizzi and his common law wife have “a combination of movable assets of R35.6 million instead of the R2.65 million declared.” The hawks calculation includes local and international assets.

DANIEL: The state’s issue is that they feel that… A didn’t disclose….// these assets the offshore assets at least were always disclosed to the correct authorities being the South African Reserve Bank as well as the South African Revenue Service. M7

VO: A brand new property worth 880 000 Euros, was paid for, in cash, by the Agrizzi’s in CASTEL DEL PIANO, ITALY.

Futhermore a total of R6.69 million was transferred either to offshore or to crypto currency accounts, and “then transferred to unknown recipients / locations”.

DEREK: Dispute figures?
DANIEL: // we haven't had a chance to go through the figures. // once Mr. Agrizzi is hopefully out of their precarious situation he's in. We can take Colonel Lazarus his affidavit compared to the figures that Mr. Agrizzi has disclosed and see if it ties up M19

VO: Witz insists that all of Agrizzi’s offshore transactions have been done within the legal framework.

South Africa is one of only 31 countries that imposes a foreign exchange control, restricting the amount of money, you can transfer out of a country. In South Africa, it’s set at R11 million.

JAMES: We are seeing a lot of people bypass foreign exchange controls

VO: James Preston is a crypto currency expert.

DEREK: CAN CRYPTO BE TRACED? (not sure where he asked this)
JAMES: // It is not sitting in a jurisdiction it is sitting in a digital space and because it was purchased in South Africa that can be clawed back from the digital space into South African authorities possession. M8 // When you start moving into some of the other crypto currencies like privacy currencies it becomes very difficult to trace M7

VO: It’s been implied BY THE HAWKS that Agrizzi systematically moved assets out of the country, in preparation for a comfortable life in Italy.

DEREK: Now Daniel took couldn't escape Greece was a tent on heading to Italy avoiding prosecution. Was that the plan.
DANIEL: //It definitely was not the plan to escape but the problem is is that they comparing Mr Agrizzi to every other notorious South African that's escaped from custody or the law or justice. M9

VO: But what is clear now, is that implicated whistleblowers might not escape the firing line.

MANDY: the investigating directorate at the National Prosecuting Authority // showed // that they no longer see him as the messenger or as a potential witness. They see him as the accused. M7

VO: According to Witz there has been no offer to turn state-witness.

DEREK: But of what is going through will be to help the state.
DANIEL: I believe there's no stopping Mr. Agrizzi. // for whatever his internal reasons are // he will continue to help the state and state capture to hopefully continue with the sweep up of corruption M18

VO: But Wiener believes this move could impact on whistleblowers coming forward.

MANDY: // because if you are somebody who has done something wrong or has some kind of proximity to wrongdoing you would look at the Angelo Gretzky case and think well I'm not doing that because they'll gun for me anyway M1




PROMOS
PROMO 1
VO: Hidden millions and an alleged escape plan – a key whistle-blower in state capture investigations now faces the wrath of the NPA in an ongoing corruption case.


PROMO 2
VO: A key whistle-blower in the State Capture Commission has landed in the dock facing corruption charges. Now his freedom is in the balance as the NPA seeks to keep him behind bars.

PROMO 3
VO: From buying an international property to stashing millions of Rands in crypto currency – why did one key State Capture whistle-blower move some assets overseas?
